chatHistory.content: Voiceover-driven wraparound animation for the x402 + Apify launch (script C2096). Not text-heavy; default style; 4K horizontal, 25fps. Full-frame opaque cutaways for the problem hook, the x402 protocol explainer (HTTP 402 / allowance / pay-per-use), and the closing CTA; transparent gaps for the on-camera speaker intros and the live Droid CLI demo, with sparse opaque callout chips over the demo ($5 USDC wallet, --x402 flag, Clockworks TikTok Scraper, 100 posts, four metrics). Orange-only, opaque cards, no fade from/to black.

scriptWithTimestamps:
00:00:00:03 - 00:00:04:13  Your agent can plan, write code, call an API — but ask it to get real web data,
00:00:04:13 - 00:00:05:19  it just fails.
00:00:05:19 - 00:00:10:13  It can't sign up for an account or type in a credit card, so that's where it quits.
00:00:10:13 - 00:00:12:19  But from today, it doesn't.
00:00:12:19 - 00:00:19:06  Hi — I'm on the core services team. I built the x402 payment flow.
00:00:19:06 - 00:00:22:06  And I'm Jacob from the AI team. I work to bring it to the Apify server.
00:00:22:06 - 00:00:28:15  Today we'll show you an agent paying for web data on a pay-per-use basis — and how much it all costs.
00:00:28:18 - 00:00:33:14  It runs on x402, the open-source payment protocol governed by the Linux Foundation.
00:00:33:15 - 00:00:41:09  The agent makes a normal HTTP call to our Actor API, and the server responds with a 402 Payment Required status code.
00:00:41:10 - 00:00:49:08  The agent authorizes the transaction and, with the x402 schema, sets the allowance — so you only pay for what the run actually consumed.
00:00:49:08 - 00:00:54:22  So this is what it looks like. This is my Droid agent, and I'll prompt it with something like this.
00:00:58:09 - 00:01:06:20  The agent finds it has the MCP installed — our custom-made MCP CLI client with x402 support built in.
00:01:07:02 - 00:01:16:01  It checks if it has balance in its agent wallet, and connects to the Apify server.
00:01:16:02 - 00:01:22:20  We see the agent has $5 USDC in the wallet, and now it's connecting to Apify.
00:01:22:20 - 00:01:31:09  The important thing: it connects with the x402 flag, telling the MCP client to use x402 payments.
00:01:31:10 - 00:01:38:15  Now it searches for the best Actor — it found the Clockworks TikTok Scraper, and tries to use it.
00:01:38:15 - 00:01:48:03  It fetches the Actor's details so it knows how to use it properly, then scrapes 100 posts.
00:01:48:05 - 00:01:55:01  The scraper is running on Apify. It fetches the data and we have it saved locally.
00:01:55:01 - 00:02:04:09  It writes a Python script to process and analyze the JSON data, and exports the summary from Apify.
00:02:04:09 - 00:02:13:11  The script finished successfully and summarizes the results — there are plenty of creators.
00:02:13:11 - 00:02:19:00  Four metrics: engagement, likes, videos, and how many plays the videos have.
00:02:19:01 - 00:02:27:01  That's it — the data is saved locally, we have a summary from the AI agent, and we're ready to use it in our workflows.
00:02:27:02 - 00:02:33:12  That's thousands of AI tools on the Apify Store that your agent can access through x402.
00:02:33:12 - 00:02:40:08  And now the agent can export to x402-enabled endpoints — monetize on Apify.
00:02:40:09 - 00:02:44:24  We really believe in the agent economy, and x402 is a critical piece of the infrastructure.
00:02:44:24 - 00:02:50:05  Read our launch blog post and docs — and give your agent the power to pay.
